stories.title: Pakistan suspends Iran trade corridors over 'security, smuggling concerns'
summary: GWADAR/QUETTA: Pakistan has suspended trade with Iran through the official Gabd-Rimdan (250) and Taftan border crossings, it emerged on Saturday.

Shahid Rind, adviser to the Balochistan chief minister on media and political affairs, said the “purpose of the temporary closure of the Pak-Iran border is to address security concerns, prevent smuggling, and make the border system more effective”.
The visit came a couple of months after it was reported that trade between Pakistan and Iran through the Gabd-Rimdan border crossing had come to a complete halt.

stories.title: Fazl clarifies he criticised policies, not institutions after ministers allege he sought 'share' in KP governance
summary: Earlier on Saturday, State Minister for Interior Tallal Chaudhry also rebuked the JUI-F chief for reportedly seeking his “share” in KP’s governance following the imposition of governor’s rule and an emergency in the province.
The Centre imposed governor’s rule and emergency in KP on Oct 11, citing the provincial government’s “deliberate disengagement” from the fight against terrorism.

stories.title: 17 dead, 25 hurt in stampede at Durga Puja gathering in Kolkata
summary: At least 17 people were killed and two dozen more injured on Saturday in eastern India after a stampede that was likely caused by sudden rainfall during a Hindu religious gathering, officials said.
In August, a stampede at a Hindu temple in Bihar killed at least seven people and injured 19 others.

Last year, a stampede at India’s Kumbh Mela religious fair killed 30 people and injured several others, and 11 fans were crushed to death in Bengaluru during celebrations for the local cricket team’s first Indian Premier League title.

stories.title: Indian airlines barred from using Pakistani airspace until Nov 24 as ban extended
summary: Pakistan has extended its airspace ban for Indian aircraft for another month, until Nov 24, according to a Notice to Airmen (Notam) issued by the Pakistan Airports Authority (PAA).

The previous extension of the ban was set to expire on Oct 24. “Pakistan airspace not available for Indian registered aircraft and aircraft operated/owned or leased by Indian airlines/operators, including military flights,” the Notam said.

On April 24, Pakistan’s top brass had announced a series of measures, including the closure of its airspace to all India-owned or Indian-operated airlines with immediate effect, as it retaliated against New Delhi’s slew of aggressive measures against the country.

stories.title: Looting, blazes and clashes in France amid nationwide protests
summary: Police and protesters clashed violently in Paris and other French cities on Saturday on the sidelines of nationwide marches against soaring inflation, with one demonstrator’s hand blown off, multiple blazes set, and looters breaking into dozens of stores to strip them bare.
Police used tear gas and water cannon against masked protesters in Paris and other cities who were throwing projectiles and aiming fireworks.

stories.title: Security forces respond to unprovoked firing by Afghan Taliban along Kurram border: state media
summary: Security forces have responded to unprovoked firing by Afghan Taliban forces along the Pakistan-Afghanistan border in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s Upper Kurram, state broadcaster PTV News reported on Saturday.

PTV News and state-run Associated Press of Pakistan (APP), which cited security sources, said the Afghan Taliban forces opened fire to “facilitate terrorists” along the border in Taldah sector of Upper Kurram.
Meanwhile, APP quoted security sources as saying that several personnel of the Afghan Taliban were “reportedly killed during the Pakistan Army’s retaliatory action along the Ghuzgarhi border”.

summary: Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX) fell 0.4% during the outgoing week, shedding 670 points, as persistent geopolitical tensions, elevated crude oil prices and concerns over a possible rate hike dampened investor sentiment.

stories.title: China AI firms eye Hong Kong listings
summary: Despite recent valuation pullbacks on data centre companies, largely originating from the US market, future AI supply-chain listings would continue in Hong Kong, said Simon Yuan, Citi's head of China investment banking.

Chinese companies plan to list in Hong Kong are cushioned by a roughly even split between domestic Chinese and international demand, Yuan, who also heads Citi's financial institutions group in APAC, said on the sidelines of the IMF meetings in Bangkok.
Next year, the focus in Hong Kong's equity capital markets is expected to shift away from pure hardware, toward Chinese artificial intelligence models and application developers, he said.

stories.title: AI-led bid-rigging alert system created
summary: The Competition Commission of Pakistan (CCP) has developed an artificial intelligence-powered system to uncover concealed patterns of cartelisation in Pakistan's public procurement market, where an estimated $60 billion is spent annually on goods, works and services.
The Bid-Rigging Detection System (BRDS) is designed to screen large volumes of procurement data and flag suspicious bidding patterns for investigation.

stories.title: India's 'cockroach' movement founder released from police custody
summary: India’s Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke was released from detention on Saturday, a day after he was detained during a police crackdown on protests against the election authority.

Opposition parties and CJP activists have defied a security crackdown, rallying to demand the resignation of India’s Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar after accusing the poll body of manipulating voter rolls to benefit Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s ruling party.

Members of Modi’s Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party have long alleged that large numbers of undocumented Muslim migrants from neighbouring Bangladesh have fraudulently entered India’s electoral rolls.

stories.title: Smiling pope returns to Vatican after cancer surgery
summary: Pope Leo XIV left the hospital to enthusiastic cheers and applause from well-wishers and returned home to the Vatican on Saturday, four days after undergoing surgery for lung cancer.

Leo’s discharge capped five days of uncertainty that rattled the Vatican and the world’s 1.4 billion Catholics, less than two years into the Chicago-born pope’s papacy, which began upon his election on May 8 last year.
Earlier on Saturday, Leo’s doctors said the pope was “fit for discharge”, according to the Vatican.

stories.title: Karachi judicial magistrate extends physical remand of anchorperson Iqrarul Hassan by 2 days

stories.title: French police clash with protesters as tens of thousands rally over cost of living
summary: Clashes broke out between police and protesters in cities across France on Saturday as tens ​of thousands of people angered by rising costs and declining public services took to the streets in some of the country's most violent protests in years.

stories.title: Trump waives new Russia sanctions as Ukraine ties slump
summary: President Donald Trump signed an executive order on Friday that waived sweeping US sanctions and tariffs targeting Russia’s energy revenues, marking a new low in Washington’s ties with war-torn Ukraine.

The move came as Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky urged EU leaders to keep financing Kyiv’s fight with nearly $80 billion more next year, insisting he was standing up for his country as Trump’s support slumped.

Zelensky asked the bloc — Ukraine’s biggest international backer — to provide more Patriot missiles to shoot down Russian missiles and come up with an extra 70 billion euros ($79 billion) in support next year to help Kyiv keep fighting.

stories.title: Egypt's President Sisi pledges to leave office when term ends in 2030
summary: Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi said on Saturday that he would not seek to remain in office when his current term expires in 2030, describing the matter as “completely settled”.

Speaking to graduates and state officials in the sprawling new city east of Cairo, Sisi said the Egyptian constitution “would not be touched”. “The period leading up to 2030 will be the end of my term as president of the state, if I am still alive.
Constitutional amendments approved in a 2019 referendum extended presidential terms from four to six years and included transitional provisions that allowed Sisi to run for an additional term.

stories.title: Egypt's Sisi seeks parliament's backing to help defend Saudi Arabia if asked

"It is inconceivable that we would allow Saudi Arabia, its security or stability to be harmed," Sisi said at a graduation ceremony ​at the Egyptian Military Academy.

Saudi ​Arabia and ⁠other oil-rich Gulf states provided Egypt with billions of dollars in aid, central-bank deposits and investments after the military ouster of Islamist president Mohamed ⁠Morsi ​in 2013.

Days after North Korea announced it had tested its AI-assisted intermediate-range hypersonic missile, Seoul test-fired its own weapon – a hypersonic glide vehicle it called a “key strategic asset capable of changing the course of the battlefield”.

stories.title: 5.9-magnitude earthquake jolts Balochistan's Khuzdar
summary: A magnitude 5.9 earthquake jolted Balochistan’s Khuzdar district on Saturday, according to the Pakistan Meteorological Department (PMD).
The PMD said the earthquake’s epicentre was located 48 kilometres northwest of Khuzdar, at latitude 28.02 degrees north and longitude 66.20 degrees east.
According to the seismological centre, the earthquake was recorded at a depth of 15 kilometres, with its epicentre located 122km northeast of Zhob.

stories.title: SSGC warns parts of Karachi may face gas supply disruption tomorrow

stories.title: Anthropic proposes law regulating AI to US lawmakers
summary: Anthropic, the creator of the AI assistant Claude, confirmed on Friday it is circulating a draft bill among US lawmakers aimed at regulating artificial intelligence to address the lack of federal legislation on the risks posed by the new technology.
Anthropic, which was banned from the Pentagon by the Trump administration in February, was forced by Washington in June to suspend its most advanced models for nearly three weeks.
Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei called on the industry last month to slow down development, fearing that a group of AI agents could take control of “the entire internet” within six to 12 months.
